title: Dedicated pools: add config schema validation library + initial policy rule set
author: Benji Okafor
description: Context: Provision-to-ready automation needs a consistent, versioned pool config format with guardrails to prevent known misconfigs (wrong CIDRs, unsafe helm values, missing runtime pinning, etc.). This PR introduces a shared validation library that compiles and enforces a JSON Schema for Dedicated pool configs plus an initial set of policy rules (“gates”) that catch common footguns before we kick off provisioning. This is the base layer for the automation pipeline; break-glass override + audit logging is intentionally NOT included here (follow-up PR). What’s included: (1) JSON Schema v2020-12 for Dedicated pool config (dedicated_pool_config.schema.json) with explicit required fields, defaults (where safe), and structured error reporting. (2) Policy rule engine that runs after schema validation for constraints that are awkward to express in pure schema (e.g., region/SKU constraints, security posture checks on helm values, cross-field invariants). (3) Unit tests for schema and policy rules (golden test cases for common failures) + a minimal “fixture matrix” covering 3 regions and 2 SKUs. (4) Example configs (valid + intentionally invalid) used by docs and operators to understand required fields and error messages. (5) Integration point in control-plane provisioning API request handling: config is validated and a normalized config is persisted; errors are returned as machine-readable codes + human readable messages suitable for CLI surfacing. Notes / design choices: Validation is split into (a) schema validation for shape/types/required fields and (b) policy validation for cross-field and security/guardrail logic. The validator returns a stable set of error codes (e.g., CFG_SCHEMA_MISSING_FIELD, CFG_POLICY_INVALID_CIDR, CFG_POLICY_DISALLOWED_HELM_VALUE) to avoid brittle parsing in the operator CLI. We also version the schema with a top-level config_version field and enforce that unknown config versions fail closed (until migration tooling lands). Rollout: This is used in the new provisioning pipeline path only. Existing manual/legacy pool expansions remain unchanged in this PR. References: ADR-0143 (config validation + policy gates) and ENG-2745. Follow-ups: break-glass override with audit trail (separate PR), schema migration helper for edge-case legacy configs, and expanding the policy ruleset based on pilot learnings.
commits: config-validation: introduce validator package and error model
schema: add dedicated pool config JSON schema (v1)
policy: add initial gates (CIDR, region/SKU allowlist, helm security checks)
control-plane: validate + normalize pool config on provisioning create/update
tests: add schema/policy unit tests and golden fixtures
examples: add valid/invalid pool configs for operators and docs
notable_snippets: Validator error format (returned to CLI / API clients): {"code":"CFG_POLICY_INVALID_CIDR","field":"network.pod_cidr","message":"pod_cidr must be a valid RFC1918 CIDR and must not overlap service_cidr"}
Example policy gate: disallow helm values enabling hostNetwork/privileged unless explicitly allowed (no allowlist in this PR).
Schema requires runtime pinning: runtime.chart_version and node_image.version must be set (no implicit latest).
test_plan: Unit: go test ./control-plane/pkg/pools/configvalidation/... and golden fixture tests for schema/policy failures. Integration: exercised via provisioning API handler tests to ensure invalid configs return stable error codes and are not persisted. Manual: ran validator against example configs under examples/dedicated/pool-configs/ and confirmed operator-facing error messages are actionable.
review_conversation: Jordan Lee: Can we guarantee stable error codes for the CLI? I don’t want the CLI to regex match strings. Benji Okafor: Yep—added a Code enum-like const set and tests assert codes for the most common failures; strings are informational only.

Vanessa Ortiz: Concerned about blocking legitimate legacy configs (we have a few pools without explicit node_image.version). Can we keep this strict but add migration guidance? Benji Okafor: Agree; keeping fail-closed for pipeline safety. Added docs note + follow-up to add a migration helper and (separately) break-glass w/ audit trail.

Rafael Mendes: Security rule: disallow hostNetwork and privileged is good, but we should also flag NodePort usage in helm values. Benji Okafor: Added NodePort gate (warn -> fail) as fail for now; if this breaks an edge case we can revisit once pilots start.

Kevin Osei: Please confirm this doesn’t introduce an override path without audit logging. Benji Okafor: Correct—no override in this PR. Break-glass + audit is in the next PR; this one only validates and returns structured errors.

Ethan Park: Nit: normalize defaults should be explicit and visible to operators. Benji Okafor: Updated normalize.go to only apply defaults that are safe (timeouts, retry caps) and included normalized output in API response when dry-run is used (wired in handler).
Jordan Lee: Request changes: add tests for unknown config_version and for overlapping CIDRs. Benji Okafor: Added both tests + fixtures; pushed update.
Vanessa Ortiz: Approved after changes. Rafael Mendes: Approved. Kevin Osei: Approved with note to ensure break-glass PR includes paging/alert hook. Ethan Park: Approved.
release_notes: Internal: Dedicated provisioning pipeline now validates pool configs via JSON Schema + policy gates; invalid configs fail early with structured error codes.
